claims.reason: Searched the full-text snapshot (whole Regulation, 88 pages): read Artykuł 7 in full (lines 2490 to 2513) and the passages on voluntariness. Art. 7 ust. 4 (lines 2511 to 2513) only names the dependence of a contract or service on consent as a factor to take into account and gives no rule on when a service must be provided despite refusal. Recital 43 in the same snapshot (lines 512 to 518) says consent is not regarded as freely given where performance of a contract is made dependent on consent not necessary for it; that is a recital, not Art. 7 ust. 4, and it is also not a rule on when the service must be available.

scope_gaps.note: That app permissions and data-processing consents are two separate things to check is the editors' juxtaposition (Ograniczenia#2 says so); each source describes only its own mechanism and none relates the two.

Editorial cost estimate. 'Część funkcji może przestać działać' is not stated by the Android page, which only says that with Nie zezwalaj the app cannot use the permission (line 37) and that the page lists how enabling each permission affects the app (line 55).

Art. 5 ust. 1 lit. c is a principle addressed to the controller of the processing (the app provider). The sentence does not say, and the snapshot does not say, that it gives the user a right to refuse an Android permission or that it governs what the permission screen asks.

Art. 7 ust. 4 makes dependence of a service on unnecessary consent a factor to take into account when assessing voluntariness (between other things); it does not say such consent is automatically invalid. The sentence says only 'uwzględnia', but a reader might assume more.

The page is Google's Polish-language Android help page (region article, 4276 of 6655 characters kept) and describes Android only; the snapshot carries a notice that the page may contain AI-translated text (line 115).
The letter C and its meaning are editorial and were not checked; only the description of the sources was checked.

Absence is claimed only for Art. 7 ust. 4. Recital 43 and other provisions of the Regulation were not searched for a rule on when a service must be available; the snapshot is the original 4.5.2016 Official Journal text, not a consolidated version.
